# How Pages lays out fonts of the Mac, as measured on the reference
# machine (DOC-05). Desk lays a family out this way whatever font stands
# for it, so its lines are as tall and as wide as in Pages.
# ascent, descent and leading are in ems: the leading is the space added
# to each line. "above" puts the leading over the text, as Pages does with
# Apple's own fonts, which have no line gap: their leading is a fifth of
# their height. "below" puts it under the text, as with fonts that have a
# line gap of their own. "fi fl" means Pages joins fi and fl into
# ligatures, and no others, as in Times and Palatino, which have only those
# two (Courier, fixed in width, has none); "fi fl ff ffi" adds ff and ffi,
# as in Helvetica Neue and its bold; "none" means it joins nothing.
# "spacing", when given, is added between letters, in ems, to bring a
# line of the free font that stands for the family to the width it has in
# Pages. No family needs it now: Helvetica Neue, which had it, is laid out
# with Desk Neue (desk-neue/), which has its widths and kerning.
# A family followed by UltraLight, Light, Medium, Bold or ExtraBold is the
# face of that weight (100, 300, 500, 700 and over, 800), where it lays
# out otherwise than the family, and one followed by Italic is its italic
# face. Pages rounds the ascent, the descent and the leading of each line
# to whole points. data/fonts/README.md explains.
# The fonts of the Pages templates have fonts of Desk with their heights
# and widths (desk-humanist/ and the others), so only the faces that Pages
# lays out otherwise than those say are here. "fifth" is a face whose line
# gets a fifth of its height above the text where its leading rounds to
# nothing, and its leading below otherwise: Didot and its bold, but not
# its italic, and the bold of Futura, but not its condensed extra bold.
# Hoefler Text gets the fifth at every size and joins ffl too.
